### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **50** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd`.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d549e24571f4f9ba947bd97d87a8d6a342dd0d45` — the merge of head `56272f193b1c6da566be15d0159ef0ca1a86b450` into base `04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d549e24571f4f9ba947bd97d87a8d6a342dd0d45 && git checkout d549e24571f4f9ba947bd97d87a8d6a342dd0d45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd 56272f193b1c6da566be15d0159ef0ca1a86b450 && git checkout -B drift-repro 04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd && git merge --no-ff 56272f193b1c6da566be15d0159ef0ca1a86b450

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 04f0cc49922b97d922084dc57d8342dc0bbb9bfd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `56272f193b1c6da566be15d0159ef0ca1a86b450`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #21289 (body and all six comments: triage `5944126361`, the question `5945481670`, the cloud reading `5945577882`, the claim `5945676057`, the dev report `5946684311`, the claim amendment `5946704697`); PR #21353 (body, the 10-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head above); the 33 check-runs on that head, re-read at 2026-10-02T06:38Z. Repo rules were read at refs with `git show`; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong:

1. **`action.ai.outputSchema`** (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`): `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` becomes `aiJsonSchemaSlot('ai.outputSchema')`, the same record plus one `superRefine`. The accept set narrows by exactly the class the cloud guard refuses: an object node whose `type` is absent carrying any of the 22 type-scoped keywords, anywhere the guard descends. **Right** — the triage ruling's shape (a refinement on the slot, ⛔ no lint rule, and none is in the diff), refusing at the subschema path and prescribing `type`.
2. **`agent.structuredOutput.schema`** (`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`, `StructuredOutputConfigSchema`): the same factory with root `structuredOutput.schema`. **Right**, and the ruling's "⛔ no copy per slot" holds: one factory, two call sites.
3. **Mirror fidelity**, judged on the diff against the cloud reading `5945577882` (cloud `main` `55f04d12`): the 22 keywords verbatim and in the runtime's order; the 5 map and 14 slot descent keywords verbatim; untyped read as `node.type === undefined`; presence tested with `k in node`, not value; `isRecord` excludes arrays and `null`, so booleans and `{}` pass; the walk is unconditional (typed parents still descended); `$ref` is not followed; visit order node, then maps, then slots. **Right — the accept set is the runtime's.** Two divergences the dev declared, judged: (a) every offender is reported where the runtime stops at its first — the accept set is identical and the first issue is the one the runtime names; right. (b) the `onPath` cycle guard — it is a descent-path set (added before, deleted after the subtree), not a visited set, so a shared non-cyclic node is still walked at every position; no JSON document is cyclic; it changes no verdict on any storable schema; right.
4. **One boundary the reading does not settle:** a map keyword holding a non-object (`properties: [ … ]`) is skipped here by `isRecord(map)`; the reading says "every value of the map is walked" and does not say whether the cloud guards a non-object map. If it runs `Object.entries` unguarded, `{ type: 'object', properties: [ { minLength: 1 } ] }` is refused there and accepted here. Confined to a value that is not JSON Schema (those keywords are objects by definition); judged acceptable, see ③.10.
5. **Public export surface: unchanged.** The new module `packages/spec/src/shared/ai-json-schema-slot.ts` exports eight symbols, but `shared/index.ts` at the head does not re-export it, `package.json` maps `./shared` to that barrel, and no `exports` wildcard reaches `shared/*`. The TypeScript type of both slots stays what it was, a record of string keys to unknown values: a `superRefine` on a `z.record` does not move the inferred type. **Right**, and consistent with the dev's unchanged `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` / `check:declaration-map`.
6. **Published JSON Schema (`json-schema/**`, an untracked build output): accept set unchanged**, because a refinement has no projection. The hand-edited ledger `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` records it: 3 new entries (`ai/Agent`, `ai/StructuredOutputConfig`, `ui/ActionAi`) and 16 new sites on 12 entries that embed actions or agents; the diff's rows sum to 19 and the totals move 212 → 215 and 616 → 635, which agrees. **Right**, and it is the ledger's own prescribed route (its header: a refinement outside the closed projection list stays here; adding an arm to that list is a public-contract decision).
7. **Every embedding is covered.** `ActionAiSchema` serves stack actions and object-nested actions alike, so `actions.N.ai.outputSchema` refuses at the nested path; the ledger's new `*.actions.element.in.ai.outputSchema` and `*.agents.element.structuredOutput.schema` rows enumerate the embeddings. **Right.**
8. **Reference pages** `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx` and `content/docs/references/ui/action.mdx`: the regenerated describes, byte-consistent with the describes in the diff. Prose; **right**.
9. **ADR-0087 D3 entry** `18.ai-json-schema-untyped-subschema-refused.ts`, regenerated into the generated region of `migrations/registry.ts` at its sorted position (before `analytics-authorable-unknown-keys-refused`). No D2 conversion is registered. **Right:** ADR-0087's launch-window clause requires a conversion only when lossless and one D3 entry in every case; supplying a `type` is not lossless — a `{ properties: … }` schema with no `type` also matches non-objects in JSON Schema, so adding `type: 'object'` narrows the authored schema's own accept set, a judgment about intent, not a rewrite.
10. **Third slot: none.** The cloud reading names exactly two readers of the one guard, so the family is closed by the runtime's own count; the dev's census of the spec's other JSON-Schema-typed slots (`tool.parameters` / `tool.outputSchema`, connector `inputSchema` / `outputSchema`, `datasource.configSchema`, the NoSQL `jsonSchema`, node-executor `configSchema`) finds none compiled by it. **Right.**
11. **Pins** (`ai-json-schema-slot.test.ts`, 24 cases, read not run): the three lists as data citing the cloud file and sha; the triage pins on both slots (untyped root and untyped child refused at their paths, the typed control accepted, a nested untyped subschema at its nested path); the ruling's additions (`$defs`, booleans and `{}`, enum-only); every keyword alone, presence-not-value, `type` present with any value, every map and slot position as one subschema and as an array, every offender, `$ref` not followed, the cycle guard. Shape **right**; the pass verdict belongs to `Test Core` (see the gate reading below).

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/21289-ai-json-schema-untyped-subschema-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, a `feat(spec)!:` title, the `**BREAKING**` banner, a FROM → TO table with the one-line fix, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and exactly one marker, `adr-0087: registered ai-json-schema-untyped-subschema-refused`, resolving to the new D3 entry. It matches what the diff publishes: one released package moves, nothing else does, so `skip-changeset` does not apply. The level is **right**: AGENTS.md reads `(narrowing)` as BREAKING, and ADR-0087's ratified launch-window level reads "pre-GA, a metadata-facing retirement or break ships `minor`, carrying the BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry"; an npm `major` is a planned act, never a side effect of one card. Gate verdicts: `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major`) concluded `success` on this head.
- **`Clause-②:` line.** PR body: `Clause-②: yes`, copied verbatim from the claim as the claim contract requires; changeset: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, where `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the arm. The arm is **right** (the diff narrows a published accept set). The value: by `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`'s criterion (does the card widen the accept set or expand the public surface?) this diff alone answers `no`, and that reader glosses `yes (narrowing)` as "widens one surface and narrows another". The `yes` stands on a different rule: `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs`'s `REFUSAL_SENTENCE` rules that a member bounded inside a bag that was a universal acceptor is not verifiable per line and "declare `Clause-②: yes` and route it to at-tier review" — which is this diff's shape (an open record of `z.unknown()` values, now bounded) and is what triage `5944126361` ruled. The declaration held the `minor` floor the level axis demands, routed the PR here, and hid nothing; `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:pm-widening-tells` and `check:pm-prior-rulings`) concluded `success` on this head. **Right.** The PM may align the body line to the changeset's `yes (narrowing)` spelling; no gate requires it.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's `open_questions` is empty. Every flag in `deviations`, `out_of_scope_findings` and the PR's Acceptance notes, answered or escalated:

1. **Body `Clause-②: yes` versus changeset `yes (narrowing)`** — answered in ②: both are read where each gate reads them; alignment is optional.
2. **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json` outside the claimed surface** — answered by the claim amendment `5946704697`; the rows are exactly the +3 / +16 the diff shows and the ledger's header mandates the hand edit. Closed.
3. **No `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment** — answered: the step-18 rationale is hand-written narrative that no gate correlates with semantic entries (`step18-rationale-merge.test.ts` checks only sort and shape); the retirement skill asks for one on a retirement, and this card retires no key; the D3 entry's own `reason` and `replacement` carry its prose into the upgrade guide. Not blocking. A one-fragment follow-up may be added in a later PR if the PM wants step 18's narrative to name it.
4. **`origin/main` moved to `04f0cc4992` after the dev's merge** — the PR reads `mergeable: true`; the one spec file among those commits is disjoint; the queue rebuilds. No action.
5. **Commit trailers and PR footer in AGENTS.md's model-free form** — outside the three contract faces. Noted.
6. **Labels** — none written by the dev; the labeler applied six; `skip-changeset` is absent, as it must be. Right.
7. **Local worktree rebuild to clear PREREQUISITE NOT MET** — no artefact of it is in the diff. No action.
8. **Stale describe and liveness row on `agent.structuredOutput`** — `agent.zod.ts:382` still reads `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced] … Parsed but no runtime consumer yet` and `packages/spec/liveness/agent.json` grades `structuredOutput` `experimental`, "no runtime reader"; the cloud reading names `agent-runtime.ts#compileStructuredOutput` as a reader. Outside this claim's surface (the `schema` slot at about `:94`) and owned by #21277 (retire or build). **Escalated to the seat:** the dev wrote "noted, not filed"; a one-line pointer to `5945577882` belongs on #21277 so the describe and the row flip or retire with that card. `Spec property liveness` concluded `success` on this head, so nothing here blocks this PR.
9. **Published `json-schema/**` stays wider than the slots** — answered: that is the dropped-refinements ledger's design; the `x-dropped-refinements` list on the 15 affected artifacts is the disclosure, and teaching `refinement-projection.ts` a recursive pattern is a public-contract decision this card does not own. Closed; no carrier needed.
10. **Mirror boundary: a non-object map value** — answered in ①.4: if the cloud guard walks an array-valued `properties` unguarded, the spec accepts what the runtime refuses, but only for a value that is not JSON Schema; no verdict moves on a valid schema. Not blocking. The cloud seat can close it with one sentence on its reading at the PM's discretion; no card.

None failed.
